subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Cams and Cranks: Converting Motion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cams and Cranks: Converting Motion.

hook.text: A camshaft turns a smooth rotation into a precisely timed push. Every car engine has at least one.

buildup.text: A cam is an egg-shaped disc on a shaft. As it rotates, its profile pushes a follower up and down.

discovery.text: A crankshaft does the reverse — it converts the piston's up-and-down motion into smooth rotation for the wheels.

twist.text: Cam profiles are engineered curves. Changing the shape changes the timing, lift, and duration of each valve opening.

climax.text: Variable valve timing adjusts cam profiles while the engine runs. It optimizes power at every speed range.

punchline.text: Spin to push. Push to spin. Cams and cranks convert between the two.

quiz.question: What is the fundamental difference between a cam and a crankshaft?
options: Cams work only at low speeds while cranks handle high speeds
A cam converts rotation to linear push while a crank converts linear push to rotation
Cams are made of hardened steel while cranks use cast iron
